Gérard Le Saint | chairman = Denis Le Saint | chrtitle = President | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Julien Lachuer]] | league = {{French football updater|Brest}} | season = {{French football updater|Brest2}} | position = {{French football updater|Brest3}} | website = {{Official URL}} | pattern_la1 = _brest2627h | pattern_b1 = _brest2627h | pattern_ra1 = _brest2627h | pattern_sh1 = _brest2627h | pattern_so1 = _color_3_stripes_white | leftarm1 = EF0000 | body1 = EF0000 | rightarm1 = EF0000 | shorts1 = EF0000 | socks1 = EF0000 | pattern_la2 = _brest2627a | pattern_b2 = _brest2627a | pattern_ra2 = _brest2627a | pattern_sh2 = _brest2627a | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = 00003a | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = _brest2627t | pattern_b3 = _brest2627t | pattern_ra3 = _brest2627t | pattern_sh3 = _brest2627t | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = 000055 | body3 = 000055 | rightarm3 = 000055 | shorts3 = 000055 | socks3 = 000055 | current = 2026–27 Stade Brestois 29 season }} '''Stade Brestois 29''' ({{Langx|fr|Stade brestois 29}}), commonly known as '''Stade Brestois''' or simply '''Brest''',''Stade Brest'', used by some English-speaking media outlets and journalists, is not a grammatically correct name for the club. is a Breton professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Brest, France|Brest]]. It was founded in 1950 following the merger of five local patronages, including Armoricaine de Brest, founded in 1903. The club has competed in [[Ligue 1]], the top division of French football, ever since being promoted to the top flight during the [[2018–19 Ligue 2|2018–19 season]]. In its early years, Brest rapidly rose in the hierarchy of regional football to the point of being promoted to the [[Championnat de France Amateur (1935–1971)|Championnat de France Amateur]] in 1958. The club joined [[Ligue 2|Division 2]] in 1970, then finally reached [[Ligue 1|Division 1]] in 1979. It experienced its sporting peak between 1981 and 1991 under the presidency of François Yvinec, playing nine seasons in the highest tier in ten years. In 1991, the club was demoted before filing for bankruptcy a few months later. The club only returned to the second division in 2004 and Ligue 1 in 2010. At the end of the 2012–13 season, it had thirteen and seventeen seasons respectively in the first two divisions.[http://www.lfp.fr/club/stade-brestois-29 Stade brestois] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120209082934/http://www.lfp.fr/club/stade-brestois-29 |date=9 February 2012 }}, club profile on the [[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] websites. In [[2023–24 Ligue 1|2023–24]], [[underdog]]s Brest achieved an unlikely third-place finish in Ligue 1 and thus qualified for the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League]], marking the first appearance in any European competition in the club's history. Stade Brestois has been chaired since 10 May 2016 by entrepreneur [[Denis Le Saint]]."}}
